title: Measurement of the patient-side quality after colorectal surgical interventions (MErkE). Clinical study for evaluation of the patient-side quality with reference to fecal and urine incontinence and sexual dysfunction after deep colorectal surgery, as compared to pre- and postoperative.
summary:
During treatment of deep-seated colorectal tumors an incontinence of fecal and urine as well as a sexual dysfunction may develop. The reason for this is the anatomical proximity of the tumor to the nerves that innervate the muscles of the bladder, anal sphincter and the genitals. During surgery or radiotherapy these nerves could be damaged and the above mentioned functional disorders may develop. As a result participating in public and social life could be limited. 
There is a little evidence as to how often this occurs. Data in medical literature are rare and of little scientific value.
Within this study patients are asked with questionnaires about their livability before and after their individual treatments.
The interpretations of these questionnaires should answer how often treatment of the colorectal tumor really leads up to the mentioned functional disorders.

interventions.name:
Observational study of patients who meet the stated conditions. Point in time of the questionnaires: 
1. round 1a: before the treatment, round 1b: after radiotherapy, preoperative
2. round 2: 8-12 weeks postoperative 
3. round 3: 6 months postoperative 
4. round 4: 12 months  postoperative

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Planned surgery of a rectal adenocarcinoma (ICD-C20) and/ or rectosigmoidal. (ICD-C19) 
- adequate knowledge of the language 
- age over 18
- a good physical and mental constitution to allow being part of the study   
- written consent of the patient
Exclusion criteria:
- age under 18
- suffering from dementia or being curated 
- missing a written consent
- occurred surgical interventions of the rectum and the rectosigmoidal passage for example rectopexy 
- occurred conventional or laparoscopic prostatectomy 
- occurred radiotherapy of the small basin, except current neoadjuvant therapy 
- anal cancer, high grade intraepithelial neoplasia or squamous cell cancer 
- status post gynecological surgery, for example ovarian cancer
